title: Pointed ambient etale lifting compatible with a changed base
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of finite presentation [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $Z,W,S_1$ be affine. Let $a:S_1\to S$ and $b:W\to Z$ be etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $r:W\to S_1$ satisfy $ar=fjb$. Choose $w\in W$, set $z=b(w)$, $x=j(z)$, $s=f(x)$ and $s_1=r(w)$, and suppose the canonical residue-field maps $\kappa(z)\to\kappa(w)$ and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s_1)$ are isomorphisms [def-weil-residue-field]. Put $T=X\times_SS_1$ and $D=Z\times_SS_1$, with fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the canonical $v=(b,r):W\to D$ is etale, and $D\hookrightarrow T$ is a closed immersion of finite presentation between affine schemes. There exist an affine scheme $X_1$, an etale $q:X_1\to T$, and a closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow X_1$ of finite presentation such that $W\cong D\times_TX_1\cong Z\times_XX_1$ compatibly with both projections. In particular, for $g=\operatorname{pr}_Xq$ and $f_1=\operatorname{pr}_{S_1}q$ one has $gi=jb$, $f_1i=r$, and $fg=af_1$, and the square with sides $i,b,g,j$ is cartesian. The map $g$ is etale and, writing $x_1=i(w)$, one has $g(x_1)=x$, $f_1(x_1)=s_1$, and the canonical map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x_1)$ is an isomorphism. Finite presentation here means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; an elementary etale pointed neighbourhood means etale with an isomorphism on residue fields at the marked points.

proof.text: By the affine fibre-product formula, $T=X\times_SS_1$ and $D=Z\times_SS_1$ are affine. Write $p:D\to Z$, $h:D\to T$ and $t:T\to X$ for the projections and the map induced by $j$. The universal property identifies $D$ with $Z\times_XT$: a pair of maps into $Z$ and $T$ agreeing in $X$ is exactly a compatible pair into $Z$ and $S_1$. Thus $h$ is the base change of $j$, and is a closed immersion of finite presentation by the two cited base-change statements.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, final paragraph; Tag 057R, lemma-lift-etale.

proof.text: The equation $ar=fjb$ defines $v=(b,r):W\to D$ with $pv=b$. The projection $p$ is etale, being the base change of $a$ along $fj:Z\to S$. Since $b$ and $p$ are etale and $pv=b$, etale cancellation implies that $v$ is etale.

source.place: Tags 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale) and 02GW (lemma-etale-permanence), as used in flat.tex Tag 057S.

proof.text: Apply the affine etale lifting theorem to the closed immersion $h:D\to T$ and the etale map $v:W\to D$. Its hypotheses hold because $T$ and $W$ are affine. It gives an affine $X_1$, an etale $q:X_1\to T$ and $i:W\to X_1$ for which $(i,v,q,h)$ is a fibre product. Hence $i$ is a closed immersion, and is of finite presentation since it is the base change of $h$. This gives $W\cong D\times_TX_1$ with both projections.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, final paragraph; Tag 057R, lemma-lift-etale.

proof.text: Put $g=tq$ and $f_1=\operatorname{pr}_{S_1}q$. For any test scheme $U$, a map $U\to Z\times_XX_1$ is a pair $(c:U\to Z,d:U\to X_1)$ with $jc=gd$. It uniquely gives $(c,f_1d):U\to D$, since $fjc=fgd=af_1d$, and its image in $T$ is $qd$ (both its $X$ and $S_1$ projections agree). The pullback of step 3 then gives a unique map $U\to W$ with composites $c$ under $b$ and $d$ under $i$. Conversely any such map has these composites. These inverse constructions prove $W\cong Z\times_XX_1$ compatibly with both projections. The defining projections also give $gi=jb$, $f_1i=r$ and $fg=af_1$.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, final paragraph; Tag 057R, lemma-lift-etale.

proof.text: The projection $t:X\times_SS_1\to X$ is etale by base change of $a$. Its composite with the etale $q$ is etale, so $g$ is etale. For $x_1=i(w)$ the equalities of step 4 give $g(x_1)=j(b(w))=x$ and $f_1(x_1)=r(w)=s_1$.

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, final paragraph; Tag 057R, lemma-lift-etale.

proof.text: The closed immersions $j$ and $i$ induce isomorphisms $j^\#: \kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ and $i^\#: \kappa(x_1)\to\kappa(w)$. Taking residue fields in $gi=jb$ gives $i^\#g^\#=b^\#j^\#$. The hypothesis says $b^\#$ is an isomorphism, so $g^\#=(i^\#)^{-1}b^\#j^\#$ is an isomorphism. Thus $(X_1,x_1)\to(X,x)$ is elementary etale with the required compatible base point.
